record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G, compute a maximum clique of G.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 38 Given a visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, compute a maximum clique of G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A simple undirected graph G = (V,E) is called a visibility graph if there exists a geometric configuration (for example, a finite set of points in the plane, a set of line segments, or the vertices of a simple polygon possibly with polygonal holes) and an assignment of the vertices of G to the geometric objects of the configuration such that two vertices u, v of G are adjacent in G if and only if the corresponding objects "see" each other in the standard sense (the open straight line segment connecting them does not meet any obstacle determined by the configuration).

A clique of G is a subset C ⊆ V such that every two distinct vertices of C are adjacent. A maximum clique is a clique of largest cardinality.

Problem. Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G on n vertices as input, design an algorithm that computes a maximum clique of G, and determine the computational complexity of this task. In particular, decide whether there exists a polynomial-time (in n) algorithm that, for every input that is the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph, returns a maximum clique of G.
artifact.status_search_result: For visibility graphs of simple polygons without holes, an O(n^3) algorithm computes a maximum clique. For visibility graphs of polygons with holes, the problem is hard to approximate within n^(1/8-ε)/4 unless P=NP. For the general visibility graph recognition input model (adjacency matrix only, with no geometric realization given), the complexity of computing a maximum clique remains open, in part because visibility graph recognition itself is not known to be in P.

status_evidence.title: Computing the maximum clique in the visibility graph of a simple polygon
status_evidence.snippet: O(n^3) algorithm for maximum clique on visibility graphs of polygons without holes.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time algorithm exists for the simple polygon (no holes) case.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Clique and Minimum Clique Partition in Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For visibility graphs of polygons with holes, gap-preserving reduction shows hardness of approximation within n^(1/8-ε)/4 unless P=NP.
status_evidence.claim: Hardness of approximation result for the polygons-with-holes case.
